qa_cases.question: Under the supplied aquatic-toxicity test procedure, what categories of information must the test report contain, and what does each category cover?
qa_cases.metadata_resolution_note: The supplied context establishes the test-report section and its contents, but not the official instrument title or date. These are therefore left unresolved.
qa_cases.reference_answer: The report must cover four groups: (1) the test substance—its physical nature and relevant physicochemical properties, plus chemical identification data including purity and, where appropriate, the analytical method used for quantification; (2) the test species—scientific name and, where relevant, strain, size, supplier and any pretreatment; (3) test conditions—the procedure and design, preparation and renewal of stock solutions, any solubilising agent, nominal and measured concentrations and their variability, dilution-water characteristics, water quality within the vessels, and feeding details; and (4) results—control validity and mortality, statistical methods and treatment of data, fish weights and growth rates, statistical results including LOEC/NOEC or ECx where possible, and unusual reactions or visible effects.

qa_cases.question: Under the supplied tariff provision for heading 2001, what minimum free volatile acid content is required for the described products preserved by vinegar or acetic acid?
qa_cases.source_title_readable: Tariff provision for heading 2001 concerning products preserved by vinegar or acetic acid
qa_cases.metadata_resolution_note: The supplied source establishes the heading-2001 rule, but does not establish the official instrument title or date.
qa_cases.reference_answer: The required minimum is 0.5% by weight of free volatile acid, expressed as acetic acid. This is a stated requirement rather than proof that every other classification condition is satisfied. The same source also states that mushrooms of subheading 2001 90 50 should not have a salt content exceeding 2.5% by weight.

support.exact_supporting_quote: For the purposes of heading 2001 , vegetables, fruit, nuts and other edible parts of plants prepared or preserved by vinegar or acetic acid must have a content of free, volatile acid of 0,5 % by weight or more, expressed as acetic acid. In addition, mushrooms of subheading 2001 90 50 should not have a salt content exceeding 2,5 % by weight.

qa_cases.question: Under Article 53 of the supplied TIR Convention, when does the Convention enter into force after the required States complete the specified signature or instrument steps, and what is the rule for further Contracting Parties?
qa_cases.metadata_resolution_note: The supplied context identifies the TIR Convention and Article 53, but does not establish the Convention's date; the date is left unresolved.
qa_cases.reference_answer: The Convention enters into force six months after five States referred to in Article 52(1) have either signed it without reservation of ratification, acceptance or approval, or deposited their instruments of ratification, acceptance, approval or accession. After that threshold has been met, the Convention enters into force for a further Contracting Party six months after that party deposits its instrument of ratification, acceptance, approval or accession.

support.exact_supporting_quote: This Convention shall enter into force six months after the date on which five States referred to in Article 52, paragraph 1, have signed it without reservation of ratification, acceptance or approval or have deposited their instruments of ratification, acceptance, approval or accession. After five States referred to in Article 52, paragraph 1, have signed it without reservation of ratification, acceptance or approval, or have deposited their instruments of ratification, acceptance, approval or accession, this Convention shall enter into force for further Contracting Parties six months after the date of the deposit of their instruments of ratification, acceptance, approval or accession.
